newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Pekao SA group creates joint brokerage.
newsitem.headline: Polish Pekao SA group creates joint brokerage.

text.p: Poland's state-owned Pekao SA bank and its group of three banks signed on Tuesday an agreement to create a consolidated brokerage house with a capital of up to 190 million zlotys, Pekao SA's president said on Tuesday.
"Today three banks and Pekao SA have signed an agreement to create one Central Brokerage House SA (CDM)," Andrzej Dorosz told a news conference on Tuesday.

He said the existing brokerage houses of the other three banks Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA (PBKS), Powszechny Bank Gospodarczy SA (PBG) and Bank Depozytowo-Kredytowy SA (BDK), would become part of the new structure. @
"The capital of the company (CDM) will come from the transfer of all the brokerages' assets and will amount to 170-190 million zlotys," Dorosz said.
Dorosz said Bank Pekao SA would have about 80-85 percent of the brokerage's capital, adding that the other three banks' capital share might be raised up to 30 percent.
He said the newly formed CDM would have a 15-percent share of the Polish investment market and with its almost 200 offices it would have the biggest service network in Poland. @
Under Poland's banking consolidation plan, the treasury handed over to the state-owned Pekao SA bank its 100-percent stakes in the PBKS, PBG and BDK.
The group had at the end of 1996 a 20.7 percent share in the total assets of the Polish banking sector and a 11.5 percent share in its combined capital.
